commits.author: trevor@twentyideas.com <trevor@twentyideas.com>
commits.subject: Add inventory format 2 record types and read compatibility
commits.body:
Introduce the canonical persisted contract for proposed/implemented technical
inventory without adding any writer: evidence references with stable IDs
unique per revision, explicit revision intent with an implemented baseline or
explicit none, delivery {repository, commit}, data entities (curated fields,
holding Component pins, owned association/production relationships), authored
ERD roots with offline SVG visuals, directory and bindings, and ERD overlays
with pins and proposed removals. Items gain documentation_view and explicit
selections.

Format 2 is opt-in: ___inventory/format.json must exist before any new kind or
intent is read, and older readers refuse the marker, the new directories and
the new Item fields rather than silently dropping them. Legacy revisions are
unchanged and read as unspecified intent. Loading validates each record
structurally (baseline must be an implemented ancestor, unsafe or external SVG
content is refused); cross-record policy checks belong to the writers.

ResolveSelection gives consumers one structural path/evidence resolver with
stable reason codes, and ComposeOverlay applies an overlay to its baseline ERD
directory without modifying the canonical record. Query and server call sites
only adapt to the Evidence type.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

Components as separate resources, owned relationships and incoming ones
derived from other entities' current revisions, and the ERDs that list
them. The ERD view inlines the author's validated offline SVG as drawn
and makes only bound elements selectable; each opens the same pinned
definition as its directory row, with focus returned on Escape. The
directory states which entities are drawn and which are not. Associations
show crow's-foot endpoints with textual cardinality, including declared
unknown; productions are labelled dashed flows, not foreign keys.
Overlays compose over their exact baseline ERD revision without
rewriting it. A drawing that fails validation at render time is refused
and the directory remains.

commits.author: trevor@twentyideas.com <trevor@twentyideas.com>
commits.subject: Author proposed and implemented inventory revisions through the public CLI
commits.body:
Add explicit `inventory adopt-format --format 2` and public writers for
Components, Systems, data entities, ERDs and ERD overlays. After adoption
every new Component/System revision states proposed or implemented intent;
before adoption format-2 content is refused and nothing is written.

An implemented revision names its delivery commit, resolved once at the
command boundary and bound to the Saga's canonical source repository. Under
the Saga lock the writer checks all-head parents, baseline ancestry, new-pin
currency (retained and self pins excepted), ERD/overlay bindings, and then
technicalpolicy.ValidateCandidate: original bytes plus delivery currency for
the entity and every implemented edge, and exact endpoint intent without
cascading promotion. Any refusal leaves no files; identical retries replay.
ERD visuals are validated and stored content-addressed in the record package.

through these writers for query and renderer tests.

commits.author: trevor@twentyideas.com <trevor@twentyideas.com>
commits.subject: Author exact Item selections and saved-view documentation pins
commits.body:
add-item, revise-item and apply-slide now accept --documentation-view and
--selections (documentation_view/selections in transactions) on
implementation and review deck Items once inventory format 2 is adopted.

A documentation pin is admitted through technicalpolicy.AdmitPin: current by
default, or, for a historical pin, only when the named saved view binds that
exact revision as its unambiguous active definition. internal/savedview loads
that view from the Saga committed at one commit of its canonical source
repository and refuses with a specific reason (unavailable/shallow commit,
Saga missing or kept in a companion repository, different source identity,
unreadable inventory); there is no fallback to a newer revision.

Each selection names a path of saved pins from the documentation pin, a
stable evidence ID and a subset range. The CLI defaults an omitted commit to
the containing evidence's commit, authors the digest of the selected bytes,
and checks every hop and the containment through ResolveSelection. Unchanged
pins and selections are retained honestly when an Item is revised, and
validate reports selections that no longer resolve or format-2 Item content
without the marker.

commits.subject: Add read-only inventory reverse-use and exact selection projections

and review deck Items and System membership, with bounded upward
traversal that reports depth, cycle and traversal cuts instead of
presenting a partial graph as complete. Superseded owner revisions are
reported but never traversed.

Resolve an exact Item selection hop by hop at its saved pins, requiring
each hop to be declared, the evidence to exist in the owner revision and
the subset to lie within it with a digest true at its own commit.
Selected-byte health, containing-evidence health and pin currency stay
separate so an edit outside the subset asks for semantic reassessment
without claiming the selected bytes changed.

Legacy revisions read as unspecified intent; newness is unknown without
a readable baseline rather than treating everything as new.

commits.subject: Filter and scope inventory reads; page declared reverse uses
commits.body:

about with their explicit intent (legacy revisions are unspecified),
identity newness relative to a named --against baseline, declared use
counts and, with --feature, the declared Item-to-member paths that put
each pinned revision in scope. --intent and --new filter only resolvable
records: conflicted or missing candidates stay on a separate
snapshot-bound unresolved page. --new requires a baseline, and a baseline
Saga that cannot be read is unknown rather than making everything new;
a baseline where the Saga did not yet exist is reported as absent.

query inventory-uses pages the implementation Items, review Items and
technical owners that declare a target, following current owner
revisions to a bounded depth and reporting depth and cycle cuts.

The comparison base Saga snapshot is located with the same same-repo and
companion-cursor rules as the change view.

commits.subject: Match Item selection projection to the records contract
commits.body:

instead of storing an evidence owner. Legacy references without a
persisted ID are not selectable: their location is no longer offered as

commits.author: trevor@twentyideas.com <trevor@twentyideas.com>
commits.subject: Report code accounted for by the technical inventory
commits.body:
query inventory-coverage measures the tracked files at one source
revision inside named path prefixes (Saga directories excluded, binary
files counted but not measured) against the unique current revision of
every active Component and System, including interaction evidence.
Each line counts once and keeps every owner, overlap is counted
separately, and stale references account for nothing. Conflicted owners
are unresolved and retired or proposed owners are excluded, each with
its reason and its own page, so absent evidence is never read as
